chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A well is drawn from, wudu is performed with it, clothes were washed from it, and dough was kneaded with it, then it became known that there had been a dead creature in it.
He said: There is no harm, the garment is not to be washed, and the salat (prayer) performed with it is not to be repeated.

Shaykh Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, may Allah have mercy on him, said: What these reports contain regarding the dropping of repetition in wudu and salat (prayer) for one who used these waters does not indicate that drawing out water is not obligatory when there is no change, because it is not impossible that the required amount of drawing out in everything that falls into it is obligatory, even though when he used it, repeating wudu and salat did not become binding upon him, because repetition is a second obligation. So it is not for anyone to make that a proof that what is meant by the specified amounts of drawing out is a kind of recommendation. Rather, what ought to be acted upon is that if he used these waters before knowing of the occurrence of impurity in them, then repeating wudu and salat is not binding on him; but whenever he used them while knowing that, repeating wudu and salat becomes binding on him. And that which indicates this is:

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ: repetition of the act, such as wudu or salat
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the ritual prayer whose repetition is under discussion
key_terms.النَّزْحَ: drawing out water from the well as a legal requirement
key_terms.بِئْرٌ: a well whose water is being discussed for ritual use
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal problem in what was done unknowingly
key_terms.مَيِّتٌ: a dead creature found in the well
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأُ: to perform wudu (ablution) with the water

ai.seo_question: If a well water was used and only later it was discovered that a dead creature had fallen into it, must wudu and salat (prayer) be repeated?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling on using water from a well that is later discovered to have contained a dead creature. The Imam عليه السلام states that prior acts done without knowledge of the impurity do not require repeating salat (prayer) or rewashing the garment, while Shaykh al-Ṭūsī clarifies that this does not negate the obligation of drawing out water from the well when applicable.
